name: Marovo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Ray, Sidney H. (1926). A Comparative Study of the Melanesian Island Languages. Cambridge. (Marovo covered; Wikipedia phonology section checked online, no stress statement)
earlier_scan.note: Wikipedia phonology sketch read: vowel length distinctive, no stress statement given.

sources.citation: Hviding, Edvard. 2018. The river, the water and the crocodile in Marovo Lagoon. In J. Wagner & J. Jacka (eds), Island Rivers, ch. 2. Canberra: ANU Press (open)
sources.note: Ethnography using Marovo vernacular terms; no orthography or stress note. Its bibliography confirms Hviding 1995 (Vivinei Tuari pa Ulusaghe, Bergen CDS), 1996 (Guardians, PIMS 14) and 2005 (Reef and Rainforest, UNESCO Knowledges of Nature 1).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, "Marovo language" (wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17); phonology section cites Hviding 1996: xxvii-xxix
sources.note: Consonant and vowel tables and 'Vowel length is also distinctive' (citing Hviding 1996 pp. xxvii-xxix); nothing at all on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1926. A Comparative Study of the Melanesian Island Languages. Cambridge: CUP — CONTENTS pages (Rosetta Project extract rosettaproject_rug_Contents-1)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.7.25)
sources.note: Contents show 'The New Georgian Archipelago 539; Grammar of the Roviana Language 543; Nduke 560; Mandegusu 562; Ganongga 565' — there is NO Marovo grammar in Ray 1926, so the earlier scan's pointer to Ray 1926 as the Marovo source is wrong. Full text (archive.org comparativestudy0000rays, HathiTrust, Google Books CHAOAAAAYAAJ) not readable by automated download (401/403).

sources.citation: Somerville, Boyle T. 1897. Ethnographical notes in New Georgia, Solomon Islands. Journal of the Anthropological Institute 26: 357-412 (archive.org)
sources.note: States that all native words in the paper are 'the Eastern, or Marovo dialect'; ethnographic notes with words; no accent or stress remark.

sources.citation: Frostad, Benedicte M. 2012. A grammar of Ughele. PhD, Univ. of Oslo (held by the project in catalog ughe1237), pp. 3-4
sources.note: Ughele stress (penult/antepenult, lexically determined) is described, but nothing on Marovo; states 'Evans and Hviding are currently working on the Marovo language' and that the only Marovo publications are Evans & Ross 2001 (OL 40(2): 269-290), Evans 2008 (OL 47(2): 383-408) and Evans 2010 (COOL 8 paper on focus). Confirms no grammar of Marovo exists.

sources.citation: Hviding, Edvard. 2005. Reef and Rainforest: An Environmental Encyclopedia of Marovo Lagoon, Solomon Islands / Kiladi oro vivineidi ria tingitonga pa idere oro pa goana pa Marovo. Paris: UNESCO (Knowledges of Nature 1)
sources.note: Bilingual Marovo-English encyclopedia/dictionary produced with linguistic input (Frostad 2012 says Evans and Hviding were working on Marovo together); likely carries a guide to Marovo pronunciation and orthography. UNESCO publications are normally free on UNESDOC, which was could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Davis, Karen. 2003. A grammar of the Hoava language, Western Solomons. PL 535 (held by the project, catalog hoav1238)
sources.note: Hoava stress only (initial stress on 2-3 syllable underived words, etc.); Marovo is mentioned only as a neighbouring language (Capell 1943 treated Kusaghe and Hoava as dialects of Marovo). Nothing on Marovo stress.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & Brian D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU (open, CC BY-SA, ANU Open Research hdl 1885/145227)
sources.note: Marovo is list no. 27 (Nggatokae/Gatukai; c. 4,500 speakers); comparative wordlists and sound correspondences only; the word 'stress' occurs only in 'It is stressed' (prose) and 'unstressed syllables' in reflex notes for other languages. No stress statement for Marovo or any language.

Only two descriptive refs, both Evans 2008 (study of one feature, morphosyntax); no phonology/grammar reference for Marovo. hh.bib adds wordlists only (Tryon & Hackman 1983, Ray 1897, Somerville & Weigall 1896, Somerville 1897, Capell 1968, Grace notebook 46).

sources.citation: Evans, Bethwyn. 2008. Subject agreement in Marovo: diachronic explanations of synchronic conditions. Oceanic Linguistics 47(2): 383-408
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The most substantial linguistic publication on Marovo by the linguist working on the language; OL articles usually open with a phonology/orthography footnote that may state stress. (Glottolog cites the Manchester working-paper version.)

sources.citation: Evans, Bethwyn. 2008. Third person plural as a morphological zero: object marking in Marovo. In C. Bowern, B. Evans & L. Miceli (eds), Morphology and Language History: In honour of Harold Koch, 281-298. Amsterdam: Benjamins
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Second Glottolog descriptive ref; may include a phonological preliminaries section. Harvard holds the volume in print (Widener Philol 37.14 vol. 298, scan-and-deliver eligible).

sources.citation: Evans, Bethwyn & Malcolm Ross. 2001. The history of Proto-Oceanic *ma-. Oceanic Linguistics 40(2): 269-290
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Cited by Frostad 2012 as one of the three publications on Marovo; comparative, may contain Marovo phonological notes.

sources.citation: Hviding, Edvard. 1996. Guardians of Marovo Lagoon: Practice, Place, and Politics in Maritime Melanesia. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press (Pacific Islands Monograph Series 14), 'Conventions' pp. xxvii-xxxii (note on the Marovo language and orthography)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only known published note on Marovo phonology (Wikipedia's consonant/vowel inventory and distinctive vowel length come from pp. xxvii-xxix); an anthropologist's orthography note of this kind commonly states where stress falls. Held at Harvard (UH Press book) and on De Gruyter; archive.org has a lending copy.
